summary: Weiqiang Wang works in linguistics, Tibetology, and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Guangdong University of Foreign Studies (2009–2013), where he became an associate professor in 2005, and served as a researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2012).
Weirong Shen is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held teaching posts at the University of Hong Kong and at Renmin University of China (~2006–2019).
Weiru Guan is a Buddhist studies scholar. He earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University, studying under MA supervisor Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).
Weizhong Huang is a Tibetologist and historian. He was affiliated with the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2012) and holds a professorship at Renmin University of China (attested 2026).

Weldon South Coblin is a specialist in Sinology, linguistics, and Tibetology who studied under Fang-Kuei Li (~1967–1972). He spent his academic career at the University of Iowa as a professor (~1973–2014) and later professor emeritus (~2014).

Wen-ling Jane focuses on Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD from Columbia University (attested 2009) under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman and also studied under Lobsang Jamspal.

Wenbiao Mai is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Hamburg, Kyoto University, and Peking University, where he received his PhD. He held a visiting assistant professorship at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

Wendi L. Adamek specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. After earning a PhD from Stanford University (-1998), she held posts at Barnard College (attested 2008) and the University of Calgary (attested 2018–2026).

Wendy Doniger is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned PhDs from Harvard (~1968) and Oxford (~1973). In 1978, she joined the University of Chicago, later becoming Mircea Eliade Distinguished Service Professor Emerita.
Wenjiang Ding was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Peking University and under Qichao Liang (~1920–1929). He later held a position at Peking University from around 1931 to 1934.

Wenjie Duan was a Buddhist studies and archaeology scholar trained at Sichuan Fine Arts Institute and the Central Academy of Fine Arts. He held multiple leadership roles at Dunhuang Academy between 1946 and 1998, including director.

Wenjie Qin works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisor Wei-ming Tu and studied with teachers Diana L. Eck, Masatoshi Nagatomi, Charles Hallisey, and Robert M. Gimello.
Wenzhuo Shi is a researcher in Buddhist studies and archaeology. Shi has been active at Ghent University as a PhD student starting in 2022 and as a PhD researcher (attested 2026).

Linguist Werner Abraham earned his PhD from the University of Vienna (~1959–1965). His career included a professorship in medieval studies and German linguistics at the University of Groningen (1971) and visiting professorships at Cologne, Vienna, and Lund.

Werner Georg Kümmel was a religious studies scholar. He held academic posts at the University of Zurich (~1932–1951), Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1951–1952), and the University of Marburg (~1952–1973).
Werner Handt was an Indologist. He studied under doctoral supervisor Richard von Garbe (~1898–1900) and earned his PhD at the University of Tübingen in 1900.
Werner Knobl is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Paul Thieme. He held an appointment as a lecturer at Kyoto University (attested 2001–2007).

Werner Schulemann was a scholar in Tibetology and pharmacology. He completed doctorates at Breslau (1913) and Freiburg (1914), worked at IG Farben (~1926–1936), and was professor of pharmacology and toxicology at the University of Bonn (1938–1955).

Werner Sundermann was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist. He held positions at the Academy of Sciences of the GDR (~1967–1991), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1970–1984), and Free University of Berlin (~1993–2000).

Werner Thomas was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Wolfgang Krause and Emil Sieg. He spent much of his academic career holding a post at Goethe University Frankfurt from around 1964 to 1988.
